title: Strengthening Daily Routines
learning_goal: Rebuild predictable routines that support child safety and emotional stability.

content.micro_lesson: Predictable routines reduce stress and help children feel safe. Even small routines—morning steps, bedtime flow, meal patterns—create stability after DFV disruption.
content.activity: Create a simple morning or bedtime routine with 4–6 steps.
content.caseworker_flags: No consistent routines at home; child showing stress behaviours.
content.escalation_trigger: Caregiver reports inability to maintain basic routines due to ongoing conflict.

title: Emotional Co‑Regulation
learning_goal: Learn how to help children regulate emotions through calm, connected responses.

content.micro_lesson: Children borrow regulation from adults. Co‑regulation uses calm tone, physical presence, naming emotions, and predictable responses to help children settle.
content.activity: Practice a 5‑minute co‑regulation exercise with your child.
content.caseworker_flags: Child unable to settle; caregiver overwhelmed.
content.escalation_trigger: Signs of severe emotional dysregulation in child or caregiver.

title: Managing Triggers at Home
learning_goal: Identify personal and child triggers and develop strategies to manage them safely.

content.micro_lesson: Triggers can be sounds, tones, routines, or memories. Recognising early signs helps prevent escalation and supports emotional safety.
content.caseworker_flags: Frequent triggers linked to past DFV events.
content.escalation_trigger: Triggers leading to unsafe behaviour or emotional shutdown.

title: Positive Parenting Under Stress
learning_goal: Strengthen positive parenting skills during stressful periods.

content.micro_lesson: Positive parenting includes warmth, clear expectations, calm correction, and predictable consequences. Stress makes this harder, but small consistent actions help.
content.activity: Identify one positive parenting strategy to practice this week.
content.caseworker_flags: Caregiver reports feeling overwhelmed or unable to cope.
content.escalation_trigger: Any disclosure of unsafe parenting conditions.

title: Strengthening Parent–Child Connection
learning_goal: Rebuild trust and connection through small, meaningful interactions.

content.micro_lesson: Connection grows through shared attention, play, gentle touch, and emotional presence. Even 10 minutes a day strengthens attachment.
content.activity: Complete a 10‑minute connection activity with your child.
content.caseworker_flags: Child avoids contact or shows fear.
content.escalation_trigger: Signs of attachment rupture requiring therapeutic support.

title: Reducing Household Stress
learning_goal: Identify stressors in the home and create a plan to reduce them.

content.micro_lesson: Stressors may include noise, conflict, clutter, unpredictable routines, or financial pressure. Reducing even one stressor improves family wellbeing.
content.activity: Choose one household stressor and create a reduction plan.
content.escalation_trigger: Stress linked to ongoing DFV or unsafe conditions.

title: Weekly Reflection & Stability Check
learning_goal: Reflect on progress and identify areas needing support.

content.micro_lesson: Weekly reflection helps track stability, routines, emotional safety, and parenting progress. Small improvements matter.
content.activity: Write a 150‑word reflection on what improved and what still feels hard.
content.caseworker_flags: New stressors, instability, or emotional overwhelm.
content.escalation_trigger: Any disclosure of new risk or regression in safety.
